title: Write merge sort
prompt: Return a new array with the numbers of values sorted from smallest to largest. Leave values unchanged. Use merge sort, and compare with the supplied before(a, b), which is true when a must come before b. The checks count the comparisons: 1,024 numbers may use at most 12,000.
hints: What is the base case, and how do you split the rest?
An array of one element or none is returned as it is. Otherwise slice it at the middle and sort each half with mergeSort.
Merge with one index in each half. Take from the right half only when before(right[j], left[i]) is true. Add what is left of either half at the end.

rules.name: sort
rules.message: Write the sort yourself. Do not call sort.

checkLabels: An empty array gives an empty array.
Use at most 12,000 comparisons for 1,024 numbers.
The array you were given must not change.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Drops what is left of one half when the other runs out.
Sorts correctly with insertion sort, which needs far too many comparisons.

feedback: Check the merge on its own with two short sorted halves, such as [2, 5] and [1, 4]. Then check that both halves are fully used.
